comparator.academicYear: Current published UvA bachelor curriculum for a Fall 2026 entrant, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official full-time curriculum supplies an exact 60+60+60=180 EC pathway. Year 1 is a shared 60-EC foundation in Dutch studies, literature, literacy, public debate and writing. Year 2 has 36 EC compulsory work, 12 EC restricted choice and 12 EC open choice. Year 3 has 30 EC open choice, one coherent 12-EC restricted-choice pair and an 18-EC bachelor project. The first two listed year-2 choices and the first-listed coherent year-3 Linguistics pair are selected neutrally; open choice remains uninstantiated.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic normalized target names no specialization. The curriculum offers four coherent 12-EC year-3 restricted-choice pairs and no pair is established as more general; the first-listed Linguistics pair is selected independently of UCR fit. For the separate year-2 two-of-four choice, the first two listed options are selected by the same neutral rule.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three feasible and materially distinct programmes are included: an integrated language-literature-communication closest match, a literature and cultural-history direction, and a public-language and society direction. They cover the evidence-backed directions at the three-alternative maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: The Art of Rhetorical Communication supplies a foundation in language use and argument, without substituting for Dutch linguistics.
Style & Meaning provides close analysis of linguistic and rhetorical choices in texts.
Persuasive Communication is the closest scheduled advanced counterpart to public debate and argument.
Creative Communication Laboratory is the closest scheduled practice in producing public-facing creative work.
Communicating the Climate Crisis provides applied writing and communication for public audiences.
Introduction to Literary Studies supplies the closest scheduled disciplinary foundation, while UCR does not reproduce Dutch-language study.
Great Literary Works develops comparative literary interpretation relevant to literature in the contemporary world.
World Myth & Literature examines how narratives acquire cultural force across contexts.
Film & Text supplies advanced textual interpretation closest to the selected theory-and-stylistics choice.
Perspectives on Literary Meaning integrates advanced approaches to language, literature and interpretation.
Introduction to Film & Media examines mediated voices and stories in cultural context.
Media & the Environment is the closest scheduled counterpart to cultural narratives about landscape and ecology.
Writing Art's Histories develops sustained critical writing for specialist and public audiences.
History Research Seminar provides the closest scheduled independent humanities-research experience.
Introduction to Western Philosophy provides theoretical analysis adjacent to the selected language-and-theory pathway, while not reproducing Dutch linguistics.
Qualitative Research Methodology directly supplies qualitative social-research methods.
Ethics provides philosophical analysis relevant to language, literature and public reasoning.
Introduction to Sociology supplies social context for literacy and participation, without being literacy studies.
Statistics & Experimental Methods directly supplies quantitative research methods.
The 12-EC UvA space is genuinely open choice, so no fixed UCR course is asserted as its counterpart.
The 30-EC UvA space is genuinely open choice, so no fixed UCR course is asserted as its counterpart.

notes.text: UvA provides an integrated Dutch-language disciplinary sequence spanning Dutch linguistics, literary history, writing and research. UCR offers substantial related study in literature, rhetoric, communication, media, cultural history and social research, but no Dutch linguistics, Dutch-language proficiency or Netherlands-specific literary-history sequence. The UCR alternatives therefore represent related academic directions rather than a full replacement for a Neerlandistiek degree.
